description: Verify that DUT discards an IPv4 packet whose Total Length is bigger than the actual transmitted data — claiming more bytes than the wire carries is malformed and must be dropped
approach:
[Objective]
Total Length must match the bytes physically present (after the L2 / Ethernet padding subtracted). A claim larger than reality means either truncation in transit or a malformed origin; either way the receiver cannot trust the contents.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet
   • Total Length = 48 (claims 48 bytes)
   • Actual transmitted bytes < 48   ← malformed
   • dst_ip = DUT IP

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any response.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT responded despite the over-claimed length. Receiver may have read past the actual buffer end (potential overread bug).

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the over-claimed packet — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT responded despite Total Length > actual data — possible overread
